title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and jailed for about six months after Fargo, North Dakota police used AI facial recognition to wrongly identify her as a bank fraud suspect. She was held nearly four months in a Tennessee county jail without bail, then about two more months in North Dakota before charges were dropped when her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee at the time. Lipps was released on Christmas Eve and later lost her home, car, and belongings.

Lipps is now suing the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck for $10 million in federal court, alleging the police relied solely on a flawed facial recognition match from a fake ID and did not investigate further or establish probable cause. The lawsuit claims the department lacked proper policies and training for the technology and that officials have not apologized. Fargo says it does not comment on pending litigation, and the case will proceed in court.
